title: RNA Extraction CTAB Protocol
author: Simon Joly
materials: Before starting the extractions Make sure all reagents are prepared, and that liquid nitrogen is available. Place water bath and vortex under a hood. Turn on water bath, add distilled water if necessary, and adjust temperature to 65 °C. Transfer the required volume of CTAB buffer to a Falcon tube (about 1 mL/sample), and add b-mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 2% (v/v) (20 µL/mL CTAB buffer). Heat to 65 °C in water bath (approx. 30 minutes). Turn on centrifuge and adjust to 4 °C. It is convenient to extract RNA of 12 samples and run a chip on Bioanalyzer per day. Prepare 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes. Two sets of tubes will be needed if samples will be ground and extracted in the original tubes. If ground tissue needs to be transferred to separate tubes, then three sets of tubes will be needed. The set used for the LiCl precipitations should be well labeled with the sample number, the extraction date, and “Total RNA”.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Workspace
steps.instruction: Prepare a clean bench and pipettes using RNAzap and autoclaved plastics. Ensure all reagents and chemicals are dedicated solely to RNA extractions and use clean nitrile gloves throughout.

steps.title: Grind Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Grind tissue into a very fine powder using super clean mortar and pestles (ideally baked overnight at 350 °C).

substeps.instruction: Keep tissue samples and tubes in liquid nitrogen at all times.
Pre-freeze mortars by filling them with liquid nitrogen and letting it evaporate.
Transfer ground powder into 2 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Create aliquots of 100 mg for extraction.

steps.title: Initial Lysis and Incubation
steps.instruction: Perform the following steps inside a hood, collecting liquid and solid waste in respective containers.

substeps.instruction: Add 750 µL CTAB + b-mercaptoethanol to approximately 100 mg of ground tissue in 2 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Immediately vortex or shake well to mix.
Incubate tubes in a water bath at 65 °C for 10 minutes, vortexing periodically.

steps.title: Phase Separation and Purification
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA from proteins and lipids using chloroform:isoamyl alcohol.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal amount (750 µL) of chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to each tube and vortex vigorously.
Centrifuge at 21,000g (ca. 14,000 rpm) for 10 min at 4 °C.
Remove the aqueous phase and transfer to a new tube, maximizing recovery while avoiding the interphase.
Repeat the chloroform:isoamyl alcohol addition and centrifugation steps a second time.
Transfer the final aqueous phase to fully labeled tubes.
Determine the volume of the recovered aqueous phase.
Add an equal volume of LiCl-EDTA (7.5 M LiCl, 50mM EDTA).
Mix gently by inverting the tubes several times.
Place tubes in a -20 °C freezer for 30 minutes to one hour (maintain consistency in incubation time).
Centrifuge for 15 minutes at 21,000g (ca. 14,000 rpm) at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: RNA Washing and Drying
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet to remove salts.

substeps.instruction: Wash the pellet by adding 800 µL of 80% ethanol.
Vortex briefly, then centrifuge at 21,000g (ca. 14,000 rpm) at 4 °C for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Perform a quick spin to collect remaining supernatant at the bottom.
Remove remaining liquid using a pipettor with a 200 µl tip.
Let pellets dry on a clean paper towel until edges begin to look slightly transparent; do not over-dry.

steps.title: RNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the purified RNA pellet in DEPC water.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 to 40 µl of autoclaved DEPC water, depending on pellet size.
Pipette water to completely resuspend RNA and place tubes on ice.

steps.title: Quantification and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Determine RNA quality and quantity using a spectrophotometer.

substeps.instruction: Treat the RNA-specific cuvette with Rnase away for 1 minute and rinse twice with Milli Q water.
Use DEPC water as a blank.
Record readings for A220, A280, A320, the A260/A280 ratio, and concentration.
Prepare dilutions for Bioanalyzer or 1% agarose gel electrophoresis (ideal concentration 100-200 ng/µL; detection range 25-500 ng/µL).
